podcast.body: Elvis Presley performed this Ink Spots song three years prior to the Million Dollar Quartet session, marking his very first recording in the Memphis studio, made for his mother. During the Million Dollar Quartet session, he played a solo version of it, showcasing the maturation of his voice and improvement in his performance over three years. "Hearing how much his voice had matured and how much his performance had improved, in the three years between his first and last recordings in that Memphis studio, since Shivers down my spine."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: In 1953, a young Elvis Presley chose to record this song, originally by The Ink Spots, as one of two tracks for a single copy record he made in a Memphis studio as a gift for his mother. This choice highlights the enduring influence of The Ink Spots on future generations of musicians. "He wanted to make a record of himself singing as a gift for his mother, and he chose one of his favourite songs. That's when your heartakes begin, as one of the two tracks he would record."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.body: The song featured on Side One of Elvis Presley's first-ever recording. This recording was made on July 18, 1953, when Presley, then a young truck driver, dropped into Sun Studios in Memphis to record a song as a birthday present for his mother. "Side one feature to song called That's When Your Heart It Begins and on the other, My Happiness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
